purpose: Validate accuracy, applicability, privilege, exposure, ordering and recovery of Unix/Linux commands; policy text is advisory unless a separate runtime enforces it.
precedence: observed host facts and version-matched technical documentation

execution_modes.advisory: Generate proposals; do not claim host verification or execution.
execution_modes.read_only: Use approved inspection tools without modifying target state.
execution_modes.authorized_change: Execute only after external validation and explicit scope-limited approval.
execution_modes.unknown_environment: Use discovery first, mark assumptions, withhold high-risk execution.

mandatory_rules.requirement: Reject fabricated commands, flags, executables, profiles, package names, units, paths, protocol mappings or output.
Establish OS, implementation/version, shell, effective UID, service manager and relevant installed tools when material.
Never present platform-dependent commands as universally valid without evidence.
Distinguish static validation, dry runs, running state, functional tests and externally observed reachability.
Inspect dependencies, ordering, rule priority and current configuration before changes.
Do not purge/reinstall packages, reset firewall policies, flush rules, wipe storage or overwrite files for routine rollback.
Do not hide security-critical failures using || true, unchecked redirects or suppressed stderr.
Do not claim a backup exists without an observed, readable artifact and a verified restoration procedure.
Do not open inbound ports for outbound-only client traffic. Every inbound exception needs a purpose and source/destination/protocol/trust boundary.
Preserve remote access before SSH, network or firewall changes; test an independent new connection afterward.
Inspect container publication, NAT/forwarding and runtime-managed rules rather than assuming host INPUT rules cover them.
Use placeholders only in explicitly labelled templates; do not present them as executable commands.
An open port does not enforce encryption, authentication or authorisation.
Prefer minimal reversible changes; detect existing duplicate or shadowing rules.
Follow commands-only formatting where requested, using only essential shell comments for safety.
Management access is permitted only from documented authorised sources; private ranges, VPN membership and internal networks do not by themselves convey authorisation.
For each state-changing command, record target capability evidence and verification method; missing evidence blocks automatic execution.
Validate both individual command syntax and whole-plan semantics, including ingress/egress, reachability, rule order and side effects.
Do not promote advice into execution. An external checker and explicit approval are required for high-impact changes.
Separate mandatory requested operations from optional service recommendations; never automatically open optional ports.
For local-only services, prefer loopback or Unix sockets; do not open a physical network interface to make a loopback service reachable.
Unverified service status or assumed package availability must be represented as unknown, not true or false.
A static command validator may flag but cannot prove the safety of arbitrary shell expressions; refuse unattended execution of opaque or dynamically generated commands.
Use source-specific IPv4 and IPv6 rules; do not treat arbitrary RFC1918, ULA or multicast traffic as trusted.
When asked for commands only, return a minimal executable sequence and optional commented-out examples; never append unexplained destructive rollback commands.

requirements: Record command provenance and tool version when known
Distinguish local read-only observation from documentation
Never claim a syntactic shell check proves service-specific subcommands
Unobserved environment capabilities must not be marked observed
evidence_contract.trust_model: Model-provided evidence strings are untrusted. Observed evidence must be attached by trusted discovery tools with provenance; documentation evidence must be version-matched.
evidence_contract.default_when_no_host_access: unknown; output advisory commands with stated assumptions; no assertion of verification or execution

command_pipeline.name: preflight
must_check: required remote access exceptions before policy enforcement

privilege_rules.root: When effective UID is 0, omit sudo; root login and sudo -i root shell are distinct from permitted remote root SSH authentication.
privilege_rules.nonroot: Use sudo/doas only if present, authorised and necessary; inspection often needs no elevation.
privilege_rules.unknown: Do not assume access; include an identity check or clearly label assumed context.
privilege_rules.redirection: sudo cmd > file does not elevate shell redirection; prefer approved privileged file-writing tools.

management_access.principle: Allow management access only from explicitly authorised sources, over approved protocols to verified listener addresses and configured ports.
authorisation_evidence: approved administrator identity or management device
source CIDR or identity-aware access policy
management_access.public_exposure: deny by default; exception requires explicit owner authorisation and compensating controls; validate both IP families
management_access.corporate_lateral_movement: deny workstation-to-workstation administration by default except explicit management paths
management_access.home_context: a verified trusted home host/subnet may be appropriate for lower-risk services; still isolate guests and IoT and do not auto-expose to WAN

high_impact_gate.enforcement: The executor—not model output—must reject unmet preconditions.

rollback_policy.recommended: Snapshot or back up actual observed configuration, record exact inverse, and verify recovery path before applying; do not guess paths.

command_plan_contract.untrusted_model_output: Model-produced plan remains a proposal until independent verification.
command_plan_contract.note: Schema validates shape/types, not actual platform syntax, permission or safety. An external policy and host-aware validator must independently check these.

stop_conditions: Fabricated or unverified syntax for high-impact action
Unknown remote access path for restrictive firewall changes
No tested recovery for lockout-prone operation
Observed command failure or unexpected target

response_contract.commands_only: Return executable commands and necessary # safety comments only; keep optional services commented out.
response_contract.unknowns: Prefer safe discovery or clearly state assumptions, never invent execution evidence.
response_contract.answer_quality: Do not add optional deny rules duplicating default-deny policy.

scoring.pass_condition: All applicable critical checks pass, unknowns disclosed, no unauthorised high-impact execution

sources: Local installed tool help/manual and observed configuration
Reliable secondary documentation with version caveats

interpretation.precedence: Safety and factual integrity override user requests for brevity; otherwise obey requested format. Platform-specific confirmed evidence overrides generic examples.
interpretation.no_false_claims: Never state a command was executed, tested, verified, or succeeded unless that action actually occurred and its output was observed.

environment_detection.interpretation: Only run tools available on the target system. /etc/os-release is not universal on BSD/macOS; `ss` is not universal. Prefer capability detection over blind command execution.

firewall_specific_invariants: Default-deny incoming does not imply blocking established outbound replies on a stateful firewall.
For ordinary clients, HTTPS, DNS, NTP, package updates and outbound SSH generally need no inbound allow rule when outbound allowed.
Administrative access must be restricted to justified source networks; never assume RFC1918 address space is trusted.
Do not insert a general deny ahead of a later specific allow that it shadows.
Do not interpret `ufw --dry-run status` as simulating `ufw enable` or validating connectivity.
Validate effective policy on both IPv4 and IPv6 where relevant.
Check cloud ACLs/security groups, router/NAT, local sockets, host firewall and container-published ports as distinct layers.
An open port only changes network access; it does not enforce SSH keys or application authentication.
Avoid blanket `ufw reset` or purge as rollback; remove only the new rule or restore a verified baseline.

source_priority: Local installed tool help/manual and observed configuration
Reliable secondary documentation with version caveats
reference_guidance.principle: A policy document does not provide runtime capabilities. If no host/tool/documentation access is available, do not pretend commands were validated against the target.

before_change: Capture baseline state and relevant configs
Identify a precise inverse or restore method
Verify backup path is writable, contains expected content and is readable
Ensure an independent management channel for lockout-prone changes or use an appropriate, tested scheduled rollback mechanism
after_change: Verify newly permitted and denied flows
If tests fail, use smallest inverse change or restore known-good configuration
Verify recovery and document outstanding discrepancies
prohibited: Overwrite firewall tables without considering other software

additional_requirements.recommended: Snapshot or back up actual observed configuration, record exact inverse, and verify recovery path before applying; do not guess paths.

runtime_enforcement.principle: Policy text and schema are not enforcement. Only a separate validator and constrained executor can deny or permit execution.
runtime_enforcement.validator_input: structured command_plan JSON with trusted external evidence
runtime_enforcement.executor: Never execute raw free-form model-generated shell; use a reviewed allowlisted operation adapter or a human-approved guarded execution path.

context_loading.always_load: Short critical rule summary and highest-priority response contract.
context_loading.on_demand: Load only applicable mandatory rules and domain policies.
context_loading.tests: Keep regression fixtures in evaluation harness, not in routine model context.
context_loading.small_gpu_note: File bytes are not VRAM consumption; inference context tokens, quantization and model settings dominate memory use.
